text:
Alice L.: quick heads-up — CI flaky on py sdk streaming tests this morning. repro (local and CI): async stream hangs on first chunk, test times out. noticed only when using editable installs (poetry install -E dev -vv --no-root) + pip editable via pipx. anyone seen import-order / auth caching weirdness?

Alice L.: repro snippet:```python
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient

async def test_stream():
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key=... )
    async for chunk in client.responses.stream(prompt="hi"):
        print(chunk)

asyncio.run(test_stream())
```

Bob K.: hmm, I saw something similar. in our case httpx 0.24 changed internal shutdown semantics for AsyncClient which can deadlock with uvloop + pytest-asyncio if the event loop policy is swapped late. Are you using uvloop in CI?

Alice L.: CI uses default loop but devs sometimes enable uvloop locally. this failure is consistent for me locally only when package is installed editable (poetry install -E dev --no-root) or when tests run with editable wheel built by pipx. non-editable wheel works fine.

Carol M.: editable installs can change import timing — if our auth caching monkeypatch runs after httpx.Session ctor, it might skip the wrapper. Could be import-order: redwood.client imports auth from .auth which patches httpx somewhere?

Sam R.: I bisected: if I import redwood.auth before redwood._client in a tiny repro it passes. if import order is reversed it hangs. so import-time side-effect. not ideal.

Alice L.: good find. so two layers: (1) httpx shutdown semantics make shutdown sensitive and (2) our auth module mutates httpx at import time which is fragile with editable installs.

Bob K.: proposed fixes: (A) stop mutating httpx at import time — expose an init_auth() and call it from client constructor; (B) pin httpx to <0.24 in dev constraints until we adjust; (C) add a small retry/timeout around stream generator yield in tests to make CI less flaky.

Carol M.: +1 to A. we should avoid global import mutations. also add explicit aclose() in client.__del__ path and in tests ensure `await client.aclose()` after stream usage.

Alice L.: I pushed a tiny branch that moves auth side-effects into RedwoodClient._ensure_auth(). also added test that reproduces the import-order failure (non-flaky). URL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3421 (WIP) :eyes:

DevEx Bot: CI queued for PR #3421 — running unit-tests, async-matrix

Sam R.: local workaround until merge: pin httpx==0.23.3 in your virtualenv and `python -m pip install --upgrade anyio==3.6.2` — that combination worked for me. also avoid uvloop in tests for now.

Bob K.: for packaging: poetry lockfiles differ on resolver v1/v2; recommend adding a dev/constraints.txt generated by `poetry export -f requirements.txt --output constraints.txt --dev` used by CI to make editable vs wheel consistent.

Alice L.: thanks all. action items: Carol to open follow-up PR to remove global httpx mutation (if my initial change doesn't cover), Sam to add constraints.txt to CI, Bob to add test coverage pinning httpx in CI matrix. I'll keep branch open until green.

Carol M.: note for types: moving auth init into constructor surfaced typing issues — typing_extensions import location changed on py3.11+ and mypy complained. fixed by adding `from typing import TYPE_CHECKING` guard and `if TYPE_CHECKING: from httpx import AsyncClient` to avoid runtime imports.

Alice L.: great — that addresses the type hints. once PR is green I'll merge and backport to the 0.1.x-maintenance branch.

Sam R.: thanks — saved me hours. posting this in #devex so others can search. :thumbsup:
